prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows an unfinished room with exposed wooden wall studs and a wired electrical box on the left about 0.3–0.6 m away (within the camera wearer's arm's reach), an open doorway in the center leading to a recessed space over 2–3 m deep, and a construction room to the right with a ladder, shovel, bucket, and shop-vac on the floor at roughly 1.5–2.5 m. In frame 1, the camera wearer's own right forearm and hammer are bright in the lower-left foreground at 0.3–0.5 m while a coworker in a yellow shirt stands on the right at about 1.2–1.5 m facing away; as the camera pans left in frames 2–4, the stud wall fills the foreground at 0.4–0.8 m and the coworker moves out of view on the right edge before frame 5 pans right and tilts down to show that coworker stepping into the doorway (~1.5 m away, facing left away from the camera) and a second coworker crouching below on the far right (~1.5–1.8 m away, about 1 m from the first worker). The depth map clearly separates the protruding electrical box and foreground studs from the backing wall and deep doorway recess—depth discontinuities that are harder to judge in the flat lighting of the RGB frames. However, the map is unreliable inside the doorway in frames 2–4, where the visible blue-lit door and floor at ~2–3 m are rendered pitch black as if infinitely far, and in frame 4 where the fisheye distortion causes the flat stud wall to appear artificially curved and dark at the bottom.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates people in the foreground and midground only in frames 1, 2, and 5, while leaving frames 3 and 4 completely blank when the camera faces the empty stud wall and doorway. In frame 1, it segments the camera wearer's right arm and hammer at 0.3–0.5 m below and to the left of the standing coworker on the right edge (~1.2–1.5 m away, partly cropped out of view), and in frame 5 it separates the standing coworker entering the doorway on the left (~1.5 m away, facing away) from the crouching coworker in the lower-right corner (~1.5–1.8 m away, facing down and left, about 1 m apart). This mask cleanly delineates the boundary between the wearer's reaching arm and the nearby standing worker in frame 1 despite similar lighting and background clutter in the RGB image. However, the segmentation map is highly unreliable: in frame 2 it misclassifies the entire wooden stud wall and open doorway (0.5–3 m away) as a single large 'oven' mask, in frame 1 it fragments the wearer's arm and hammer into overlapping 'person' masks with floating labels at the top, and across all frames it misses the electrical box, shop-vac, bucket, shovel, and ladder.
descriptions.pose: The skeleton map detects body keypoints only in frames 2 and 5 and detects no hand keypoints (magenta) in any frame, even when the camera wearer's hand holding the hammer is at 0.3–0.5 m in frame 1. In frame 2, a partial yellow torso-and-head skeleton on the far right edge at ~1.2–1.5 m shows the coworker cropped by the frame boundary, facing away and to the left of the camera wearer; after vanishing in frames 3 and 4 as the camera turns toward the wall, a fuller upper-body and head skeleton appears in frame 5 at ~1.5 m, angled downward and to the left into the doorway with the head turned away from the camera wearer. The skeleton in frame 5 makes the coworker's shoulder-to-hip tilt and forward-leaning torso orientation inside the dark doorway easier to read than in the RGB frame alone. However, the pose map is unreliable where people are partially occluded or cropped by the frame edges, completely missing the coworker in frame 1, the camera wearer's own arm and hand in frames 1 and 2, and the second coworker crouching in the lower-right corner of frame 5.
